slot.brief: Use bond enthalpies of reactants and products to compute ΔH of a combustion/formation reaction via Hess-type addition.

stem:
Given the following thermochemical data:
$$\begin{aligned}
\Delta_{\text{sub}}H^\circ[\text{C}(s)] &= 715\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1} \\
\text{B.E.}(\text{H}-\text{H}) &= 436\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1} \\
\text{B.E.}(\text{C}-\text{H}) &= 414\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1} \\
\text{B.E.}(\text{C}\equiv\text{C}) &= 828\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$$
The standard enthalpy of formation ($\Delta_f H^\circ$) of ethyne, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2(g)$, is:

verdicts.working: Formation: 2C(s) + H2(g) → C2H2(g). ΔfH = 2·ΔsubH(C) + BE(H–H) − [BE(C≡C) + 2·BE(C–H)] = 1430 + 436 − (828 + 828) = +210 kJ/mol.

working:
The standard reaction for the formation of ethyne from its elements in their standard states is:
$$2\text{C}(s) + \text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_2(g)$$

Using a Hess's Law cycle, $\Delta_f H^\circ$ is given by the enthalpy required to atomize the reactants minus the bond enthalpies of the bonds formed in the product:
$$\Delta_f H^\circ = \sum \Delta H_{\text{atom}}(\text{reactants}) - \sum \text{B.E.}(\text{products})$$

1. Enthalpy required to atomize reactants:
- Sublimation of $2\text{C}(s)$: $2 \times \Delta_{\text{sub}}H^\circ[\text{C}(s)] = 2 \times 715 = 1430\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
- Dissociation of $1\text{H}_2(g)$: $1 \times \text{B.E.}(\text{H}-\text{H}) = 436\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
$$\text{Total for reactants} = 1430 + 436 = 1866\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

2. Enthalpy released upon forming bonds in $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2(g)$ (structure is $\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{H}$):
- $1 \times (\text{C}\equiv\text{C})$ bond: $828\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
- $2 \times (\text{C}-\text{H})$ bonds: $2 \times 414 = 828\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
$$\text{Total for products} = 828 + 828 = 1656\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

3. Enthalpy of formation:
$$\Delta_f H^\circ = 1866 - 1656 = +210\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Independent check: Formation: 2C(s) + H2(g) → C2H2(g). ΔfH = 2·ΔsubH(C) + BE(H–H) − [BE(C≡C) + 2·BE(C–H)] = 1430 + 436 − (828 + 828) = +210 kJ/mol.
